reviews.title: Stay away total bait and switch
reviews.text:
DOWN markets itself as honest and “now or never.” The product does the opposite.
Every serious dating app that charges for outgoing messages shows last active, or at least “online now / recently.” That’s basic. You don’t pay to talk to a profile that hasn’t been opened in six months. DOWN won’t timestamp anyone. Their excuse is that everyone in Nearby has been on recently, so they don’t need to show it. If that’s true, putting a stamp on it costs them nothing. They don’t, which means you have no idea if the person you’re looking at was on an hour ago or last year.
I tested it the way a normal user would. First I only swiped Down on younger women who looked active. Then I opened it up to every age just to see if the app was dead or just dead in one lane. About 300 Downs. Not one match. Not one profile view from anyone I swiped on. If 300 people actually received those and all passed, you’d still expect a handful of curiosity views. I got none.
So you’re left with two options, and neither is good for the user:
1.  The “nearby / recently active” claim is false, and you’re swiping on stale or unused profiles.
2.  The app is not actually delivering your interest to real people, and the match/view counters are theater.
Either way, hiding last-seen while charging to reach people is the scammy part. If they wanted trust, they’d show activity like everybody else and let the profiles speak. They don’t, because the second you can see who hasn’t been on in months, the feed looks empty.

reviews.title: Paying to Stay Restricted
reviews.text:
I regret subscribing to this app.
They market it like you should “give it 3 months,” but once you pay, you realize how limited everything actually is. As a paying user, you get only one flirt per day. That means you still cannot freely message people you are genuinely interested in or have any real flexibility.
If you want better chances, you are pushed to pay even more for additional flirts despite already having a subscription. So you are paying and then asked to pay again. That feels predatory.
What exactly are we paying for?
There are barely any real matches. And when you do match, most accounts do not respond. It feels like inactive profiles or bots. The like system does not make sense if you cannot realistically turn interest into actual conversations.
Compared to other dating apps, this is by far the worst value for a paid subscription. On other platforms, once you subscribe, you can message freely and at least have a fair shot. Here, it feels like you are paying just to stay restricted.
What annoyed me most is that instead of improving the matching system or overall experience, the app sends motivational quotes and dating tips. I am not frustrated because of rejection. I am frustrated because there are no real opportunities to connect in the first place. Tips do not fix a broken system.
After one month, I realized it simply was not worth continuing.
If you are thinking about subscribing, understand that paying does not unlock a real or flexible dating experience here.

reviews.title: No selection. Don’t pay
reviews.text:
I tried the service and after a few swipes I ran out. So I paid for the VIP service. In less than an hour, there were no more locals in my area. I live near San Jose California and my local area is 60 miles. They were showing me locals that were well over 100+ miles away.
They sell the ability to communicate with other people instead of just swiping on them, which is an additional charge on top of the VIP membership, which makes no sense because I don’t understand other than the unlimited swiping what I’m really getting when there’s nobody to swipe on.
Don’t waste your time paying for this unless you are either in Los Angeles or New York. 
As far as the developers go, my message to you is try to get people to have as many connections as possible before charging for this paid service in addition to the membership fee. When people actually see it’s working the word-of-mouth will justify the fees. Right now it does nothing and for that I highly do not recommend your product.

reviews.title: Kind of fun, but another app gatekept by money.
reviews.text:
So, if you have “50 likes” whose names you can actually see in the list, and the fyp only refreshes the same unrelated 30 names, and the list doesn’t change s single time when I get an “update” notification every day…

That means that no matter who you are or how many people are interested in you, you will not be able to access 90% of them unless you pay, no matter how you swipe. 

This is a major, pretty obvious problem that I’m pretty sure they are counting on people to just not understand or game out themselves. 

There’s really only two reasons for this to occur:
- There are not enough requested profiles available & signed up for what you’re looking for, and these folks know that
- The app owners are purposefully gatekeeping 90% of your responses behind a premium membership.

If it’s the first option, then you are being purposefully misled into assuming there are more profiles available than the reality. 

If it’s the second option, you deserve to know that this is something that won’t be effective unless you pay—and there’s no guarantee that there’s enough people to even have any more to add if you do pay. You could pay and not see a new profile for weeks, let alone one that applies to you. 

None of this touches on the amount of bots and pretty obvious scam accounts that also clog a feed for weeks. 

Otherwise, neither option is defensible, in my opinion, so I felt like explaining them.

reviews.title: No honestly
reviews.text:
This site is an absolute scam. I was told to complete a survey to receive 3 days of free premium/VIP, and I was also pressured to leave a positive review as part of the deal. I did exactly what they asked — filled out the survey and left a good review — and guess what? No free VIP. Nothing.

They straight-up lied to get a good review and never delivered what they promised. This is classic bait-and-switch behavior and completely dishonest. If a company has to trick users into leaving fake positive reviews, that tells you everything you need to know.

Do NOT waste your time or money here. If they’re willing to scam you over something small like a 3-day trial, imagine what else they’ll do. Avoid this site at all costs.
